key_insight: WaferTetris explores freeform application mapping on wafer-scale accelerators instead of relying on fixed geometric templates. The goal is to give workloads more flexibility in how they use the wafer’s massive compute capacity.
problem_solved: Mapping applications across hundreds of thousands of interconnected processing elements is difficult. Existing template-based approaches simplify programming but restrict the layouts available to workloads.
method: Target application mapping across a wafer-scale network of processing elements.
Explore freeform layouts beyond the fixed geometric constraints of template-based mappings.
Specific algorithms and evaluation results are not available in the supplied, truncated abstract.
impact: More flexible mapping could help AI/ML workloads make better use of wafer-scale hardware. The supplied excerpt does not establish measured performance or efficiency gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side wafer grids contrasting fixed geometric templates with illustrative freeform mappings.
A zoomed-in wafer diagram showing processing elements and their interconnections.
A workflow diagram connecting an application graph to its placement on the wafer.
Icons highlighting mapping flexibility, programming complexity, and compute utilization.
paper_title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators
paper_authors: Dayou Du, Congjie He, Andrew Boutros, Luo Mai, Vaughn Betz
